title: Socket pool tuning and retry/backoff alignment to mitigate Hosted API 5xx/timeouts during escalations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Several customers reported prolonged 5xx waves and high request latencies during a tenant surge. Investigation shows a confluence of socket pool exhaustion, suboptimal keepalive settings, and misaligned retry jitter between SDKs and the gateway that amplified retry storms and produced timeouts. This ticket scopes a targeted mitigation: tune socket/connection pooling, align client+gateway retry semantics (backoff and idempotency gates), and add per-tenant egress/connection telemetry + safeguards to prevent recurrence.
technical_summary: Root cause: (1) upstream connection pool limits on proxy nodes were reached under a tenant burst because connections leaked on high tail latencies; (2) the SDK retry logic and gateway retry/circuit-breaker windows used different backoff bases and no jitter, causing synchronized retries; (3) for some Private/VPC customers NAT gateway ephemeral port limits exacerbated egress failures, surfacing as 502/504. We will implement: connection pool hard limits + LRU eviction, stricter idle keepalive and TCP reuse tuning, add randomized exponential backoff (per SDK + gateway) with client-visible idempotency headers, and per-tenant in-flight request caps with graceful 429s instead of cascading 5xx.
acceptance_criteria: New connection pool config deployed to proxy+gateway with default in-flight cap of 250 per host and LRU eviction verified in staging
SDKs and gateway both use exponential backoff with jitter; documented contract for idempotency header checked into SDK repos
Per-tenant in-flight metrics (connections, sockets, ephemeral port usage) visible in Console; alerts trigger before 80% of configured limits
No customer-observable 5xx spikes in 48h post-deploy during a synthetic tenant surge replay in perf lab
rollout_plan: Stage: deploy pool/keepalive config to staging cluster; run tenant-surge load test (10k concurrent tenants) and gather socket metrics
Canary: push to 10% of hosted production traffic (non-critical tenants) for 4 hours; monitor error rate, P95 latency, connection-states
Ramp: 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 24-48h if metrics stable; enable per-tenant caps with permissive logging first, then enforce
SDK: release patch versions for node/python/go with backoff/jitter defaults and announce compatibility contract
rollback_plan: If canary shows >2x baseline 5xx or P95 latency regression >20% for 30+ minutes, revert pool config and disable per-tenant enforcement; fall back to previous routing policy and open incident for deeper RCA.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana dashboards: proxy-sockets-per-host, ephemeral-port-usage-by-subnet, per-tenant-inflight-requests
Alert: TenantInflightRequests > threshold => P2 pager and automated request-shedding to 429 for offending tenant
Add trace tags for 'retry-cause' and 'idempotency-key' to span data for better postmortem correlation
postmortem_notes: Customers affected: 3 enterprise tenants during 2026-01-12 surge
Immediate mitigations: increased proxy worker count (hotfix) and enabled short-term request queueing at edge
Learnings: per-tenant egress constraints (NAT port exhaustion) should be surfaced in Console; SDKs must default to jittered backoff to avoid sync replays
Follow-ups: add NAT/egress advisories to Private deployment checklist; run annual tenant surge drills
